result:
No actions yet. There's nothing to read beyond the spreadsheet description, and nothing should be built before we've talked.

---

Thanks for pasting the spreadsheet layout. That gives me a good starting point.

Right now each row records one loan: which seed, how many packets, who took them, and when they went out and came back. One thing stands out: about a third of the "Date back" cells are empty. That could mean a lot of seed is still out. It could mean seeds came back and nobody wrote it down. Or, as in many seed libraries, it could mean people were never really expected to return the same packets, and are meant to bring back seed saved from their own harvest instead.

Which of those it is changes what we'd build. If it's mostly unlogged returns, you probably want something that makes recording easy at the table. If it's seed that's genuinely overdue, you probably want reminders and a clear list of who has what. If "coming back" means saved seed from a later season, then a return may not match a loan at all, and that's a different kind of record.

So before anything else: when you look at those empty "Date back" cells, what do you think is actually behind most of them, and what problem has that caused for the library?
